messages:
ana: ran an nsys + perfetto pass on the 8xA100 repro from yesterday. seeing repeated NCCL all-reduce windows that coincide with KV cache syncs — looks like cache eviction paths are forcing CPU/GPU memcpy while the all-reduce is running. attaching perfetto timeline link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 :eyes:

kevin: can you paste the nsys command you used? wondering if nvtx ranges were emitted for the KV ops.

ana: command was:```nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl --output=8x_kv_nccL.nsys python -u run_profile.py --model gpt-large --batch 32 --tp 2 --pp 4``` I added NVTX around kv_write/kv_read and around kernel_selector.

sam: quick read: if kv_write is synchronous we will serialize with nccl if they share the same stream. did you see multiple CUDA streams being used?

ana: timeline shows three streams: compute (default), async-copy, nccl. but the async-copy bursts align with all-reduce start causing reduced overlap. SM utilization drops ~25% during these bursts.

perf-bot: summary metrics from the trace: p50 token latency +9%, p95 +18% vs baseline; all-reduce avg time 12.8ms -> 18.6ms during KV-warm; memcpy H2D increased by 1.6x; NCCL op overlap with compute reduced from 42%->12%.

maria: did you try disabling prefix KV persistence (inference-only warm cache) to see if writes are the culprit? also share the small log snippet where we log kv_cache hits/misses.

ana: repro toggles: with kv_persist=false the all-reduce windows shrink and p95 goes down by ~10%. log snippet:```[2026-06-05 14:02:12] kv_cache: miss key=batch_001, size=24MB -> scheduling write to GPU async-copy stream
[2026-06-05 14:02:12] nccl: all_reduce start seq=542
[2026-06-05 14:02:12] cuda memcpy H2D queued on async-copy stream```

kevin: this smells like stream contention: NVLINK peer copy + NVSHMEM? what is the copy mechanism for KV writes — cudaMemcpyAsync into GPU or staging on host then NCCL?

ana: KV writes go host->GPU via cudaMemcpyAsync into dedicated async-copy stream, then we signal compute. NCCL uses its own streams. but GPU memory pressure causes page migration fallback occasionally so the async-copy becomes more expensive.

nick: experiments to try: 1) move KV writes to a dedicated pinned buffer pool and pre-post; 2) change NCCL algorithm to TREE to see if that reduces all-reduce tail; 3) throttle batching window so we don't create big concurrent KV writes during canary spikes.

sam: also consider kernel_selector fallback — I saw that our new selector prefers a fused-kernel when seq_len<512, but that kernel triggers larger temp buffers for KV ops. try forcing the older kernel for a run.

ana: good catch — I re-ran with KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy and the all-reduce + memcpy overlap improved; p95 dropped ~12% vs patched selector. will bisect selector change that introduced larger temp buffers.

maria: file a perf regression ticket and attach nsys export + perfetto UI slices. include the small reproducer script and the exact env flags you used.

ana: filed PERF-984 with trace attachments and quick reproduce command. link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/PERF-984

kevin: short-term mitigation: make KV writes async but limit concurrency (max 2 concurrent writes), or push KV flush to lower-priority CUDA stream that NCCL doesn't block on. Also adding an NVTX range around all-reduce helps with tracing/priority in some drivers.

nick: I'm going to try switching NCCL_ALGO=ring and NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD=0 on a staging run to see if the pattern changes. will post results later today.

ana: thanks — next steps: (1) bisect kernel_selector change for temp buffer regression, (2) experiment with KV pinned pool + limited concurrent writes, (3) test NCCL algos. timeline + trace artifacts are in PERF-984.

perf-bot: note: tagging eng-sre for possible driver-level fallback work if pinned allocation doesn't fix page migration spikes. @eng-sre :wave:
